eligibility_reason: Within-paper-only replication: the paper's 'replication sample' (EGCUT de novo and in silico genotyping, N = 5949 + 536) tests the ABCC9 rs11046205 association discovered in this same paper's own GWAS meta-analysis ('The data of the individual GWAS regarding sleep duration are reported here for the first time'), not a separately published finding; no prior published finding is replicated with new data.
notes: Candidates considered and rejected: (1) The discovery->replication design (Results: 'found no significant association with SDav in the replication sample'; later meta-analysis of the early-chronotype winter subgroup 'validated the association', P = 7.9e-8) replicates the paper's own discovery-phase result, i.e. a within-paper replication; excluded by the codebook. (2) Prior CLOCK gene association (Allebrandt et al. 2010, Biol Psychiatry, ref 9): explicitly NOT tested - 'earlier associations could not be followed up because of low-quality imputation in the region'. (3) DEC2 (He et al. 2009, ref 14): only discussed ('rare variants with large effects ... will not explain the variation'), not tested. (4) Hyperkinetic/Drosophila sleep (Bushey et al. 2007, ref 37): Discussion says 'Our study supports the role of Hyperkinetic in modulating sleep duration, as its human homologue, KCNAB1, is the second best signal in the discovery meta-analysis' - a post hoc cross-species consistency remark on a sub-genome-wide-significant locus (P = 2.60e-6 / 8.41e-7), not a designed replication test; a liberal second coder might read it as a conceptual replication, hence a low-probability alternative reading. (5) The Drosophila dSur RNAi knockdown is a new functional experiment corroborating the paper's own GWAS hit, not a replication of a published finding. (6) 'Technical replication' with a perfect-proxy SNP (rs11046209) is a genotyping/statistical replicate, not a replication of a prior finding. Eligibility judged fairly clear; gt_ambiguity for the negative call: clear (minor risk from item 4).
